THE PEPTIDE INDEX · COGNITION

Selank

A peptide with real human anxiety research—and a nootropic reputation that runs ahead of it.

Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide studied primarily in Russian clinical literature for anxiety-related disorders. Human data exist, but they are small, geographically concentrated and do not validate the broader cognitive-enhancement claims common in biohacking culture.

EDITORIAL VERDICT
Human signal exists. Broader cognition claims remain uncertain.

The strongest defensible story is anxiety—not generalized cognitive enhancement.

HUMAN RESEARCH

●●●○○

Small comparative clinical studies exist in anxiety-related populations.

THE GAP: MEANINGFUL — The community story extends well beyond the narrow human clinical literature.
01 / WHAT IT IS

A narrower evidence story than its reputation.

Selank is a seven-amino-acid synthetic peptide (TKPRPGP). Its clinical literature is centered on anxiolytic effects rather than broad cognitive enhancement.

Reduced anxiety can improve perceived concentration without demonstrating a direct nootropic effect.

02 / HUMAN EVIDENCE

There is a signal—but the evidence base is small.

A 2008 comparative study enrolled 62 patients with generalized anxiety disorder and neurasthenia: 30 received Selank and 32 medazepam. The authors reported similar anxiolytic effects, with additional antiasthenic and psychostimulant effects in the Selank group.

A later study compared phenazepam monotherapy in 30 patients with combined Selank plus phenazepam in 40 patients with anxiety-related disorders.

What this supports: a legitimate human anxiety signal.
What it does not support: treating Selank as a broadly proven cognitive enhancer.
03 / COMMUNITY SIGNAL

The community often turns anxiolysis into “nootropics.”

Public discussion frequently describes calmness, focus, reduced anxiety and clearer thinking.

Community ≠ Clinical Guidance. Subjective reports can identify themes; they cannot establish efficacy or safety.

Explore Community Pulse →

04 / CLAIM VS EVIDENCE

Where the story gets stretched.

“Selank is a proven nootropic.”Too broad. Human literature is more defensible around anxiety-related outcomes.
“Reduced anxiety proves better cognition.”No. Subjective focus and objective cognitive performance are different outcomes.
“Human studies mean the evidence is strong.”Sample size, replication, geography and methodology matter.
05 / SAFETY + REGULATORY

Human exposure exists. Important uncertainties remain.

FDA currently lists Selank acetate among bulk substances for which compounded products may pose immunogenicity risk for certain routes because of aggregation and peptide-related impurities, and states that it lacks important safety information regarding Selank acetate administered to humans.

Selank is not an FDA-approved drug. Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved or reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality before marketing.

06 / THE GAP

MEANINGFUL

This is not a case of “no human evidence.” It is a limited human anxiety signal being generalized into a much larger cognitive-enhancement narrative.
